talking_points.headline: Banks scale AI agents in compliance — but 90% are still stuck in pilot
talking_points.context_html: McKinsey estimates a single compliance officer could soon supervise 15–20 AI agents, unlocking productivity gains of up to 20x on tasks like KYC screening and due diligence — yet only around 10% of financial institutions have moved agents into production. For Adam's change agenda, this is the clearest signal yet that AI-enabled operating-model redesign, not just tool adoption, is becoming the real compliance battleground; WPB's own KYC and onboarding workflows are exactly the high-volume, rules-based processes this wave targets.
source_links: AI agents move from pilot to workforce

talking_points.headline: Wealth-tech vendors race to build AI 'orchestration' layers for advisers
talking_points.context_html: Playbook (formerly Powder), led by Kanishk Parashar, Founder and CEO, launched an AI orchestration platform now used by roughly 40 wealth firms managing a combined $660 billion in client assets, automating onboarding, proposals and compliance reviews from plain-English instructions. It's the latest sign the wealth-tech AI layer is consolidating around orchestration rather than point tools — a build-vs-buy question Adam's team will face as HSBC's own AI initiatives mature.

talking_points.headline: Held-away assets are private banking's data blind spot — and its next AI use case
talking_points.context_html: A new industry analysis flags that clients' assets held outside a bank's own platform routinely go untracked, weakening suitability assessments and cross-sell economics at exactly the moment banks are racing to deepen share of wallet. It's a sharper version of the completeness problem HSBC's own PRISM (Aladdin-based) advisory tooling was built to help close — the gap isn't model quality, it's visibility into assets the bank never sees in the first place, which is a data-aggregation and client-disclosure problem before it's an AI problem.
source_links: Wealthy clients' hidden assets blind spot

AI & Technology.title: AI agents move from pilot to workforce in bank compliance
AI & Technology.summary: Banks are deploying specialised AI agents to automate compliance work such as KYC screening and due diligence, with McKinsey estimating productivity gains of up to 20x when one compliance officer supervises 15-20 agents. Only about 10% of financial institutions have scaled AI agents into production so far, though fraud detection and customer onboarding are top priorities; one platform cited cut onboarding from eight days to under a minute. For Adam, this is the clearest signal yet that AI-enabled operating-model redesign is becoming the real compliance battleground, and WPB's own KYC and onboarding workflows are exactly the high-volume, rules-based processes this wave targets.

AI & Technology.title: Playbook launches AI orchestration platform for wealth management firms
AI & Technology.summary: Wealth-tech firm Playbook (formerly Powder) launched an AI orchestration platform that lets RIAs, family offices and wealth managers automate workflows including client onboarding, proposal creation, estate planning analysis and compliance reviews using plain-English 'plays.' The platform already serves roughly 40 firms representing about $660 billion in combined client assets, with founder Kanishk Parashar positioning it around cost, quality and ROI optimisation. It's a further sign the wealth-tech AI layer is consolidating around orchestration rather than point tools — a build-vs-buy question relevant as HSBC's own AI initiatives (Wealth Intelligence, Model ML) mature.

Private Banking & Wealth.title: Wealthy clients' hidden assets are banks' biggest blind spot
Private Banking & Wealth.summary: A new analysis argues that wealthy clients' undisclosed or poorly tracked assets held outside a bank's core wealth platform represent a significant blind spot for private banks trying to build a complete picture of client wealth. The gap undermines suitability assessments and cross-sell opportunities as banks compete for a greater share of client wallets, and the piece calls for better data-aggregation tools to surface held-away assets. This directly touches WPB's share-of-wallet ambitions in Asia — the same completeness problem PRISM/Aladdin-based advisory tools are meant to help close, but only for assets banks can already see.

Regulatory & Markets.title: Hong Kong stocks fall Friday as tech and property shares weigh on market
Regulatory & Markets.summary: Hong Kong stocks closed lower on Friday as technology and property shares weighed on the market, diverging from broader gains elsewhere in Asia. CK Hutchison fell 3.4% after its H1 2026 results, while investors digested Tencent's Q2 earnings and continued optimism around Shein's planned Hong Kong IPO. A soft session in HSBC's home market, though driven by idiosyncratic single-stock moves rather than a broad risk-off shift.
